notes: Fixtures are generated by setup_fixtures.sh, not committed (default /tmp/opencode/architecture-viz-evals); replace <fixture> in each prompt with that path. Run pattern (skill-creator): per eval, spawn one subagent with the current SKILL.md + scripts and one with a baseline snapshot of the previous SKILL.md, give both the same prompt, point each at its own copy of the fixture, and have each write artifacts into its copy's docs/. Save each report under iteration-N/<eval>/<config>/outputs/ and grade against the assertions below with text/passed/evidence plus summary.pass_rate.

evals.name: eval-0-standard
evals.prompt: Map out the architecture of the project at <fixture>/fixture-app - dependency graph, boot flow, the works - and give me one HTML file I can open in a browser.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained HTML at <fixture>/fixture-app/docs/architecture.html: hand-authored SVG graph with >=4 g.n nodes and >=3 labeled edges, a boot sequence, subsystem panels, watch items with path:line evidence, footer. Checker clean; render PNG produced.
assertions: Writes a single self-contained HTML file at `<fixture>/fixture-app/docs/architecture.html` with no external CDN/webfont/script references.
The SVG graph contains at least 4 `g class="n` node groups and at least 3 `path class="edge"` edges, each edge carrying an attached `text.elabel` label.
Every node and every Watch item carries a `path:line` evidence reference into the fixture source (e.g. `src/services.py:12`).
Runs the skill's checker and quotes a clean result (exit 0 with a `clean: ... N nodes, M edges, K labels` line), not merely a claim that it is clean.
Produces a rendered PNG (render-check.sh exit 0 and/or a reported PNG path).

evals.name: eval-1-honest-gaps
evals.prompt: Map the architecture of <fixture>/fixture-app but keep it honest - call out the dead code and anything inconsistent so we can use it in a refactor plan.
evals.expected_output: An architecture map whose Watch items name the planted gaps (src/legacy.py is dead/unreferenced; the config default is duplicated) with severity and path:line, and whose graph reflects the real wiring.
assertions: Watch items list the planted gap that `src/legacy.py` is dead/unreferenced (or the duplicated config default), each with a severity and a `path:line` reference.
Does not fabricate gaps: every Watch item resolves to a real fixture file/line, with no invented modules or files.
The graph reflects the real wiring (`bootstrap` constructs `config`/`store`/`engine`/`services`; `cli` consumes `bootstrap`), not a generic diagram.
Checker runs clean and a render is attempted, with both results stated.

evals.name: eval-2-nontrigger-chart
evals.prompt: Take the test counts in <fixture>/fixture-app and turn them into a bar chart I can drop into the README.
evals.expected_output: Routes to a data-chart skill (create-viz), not architecture-viz: no architecture map / SVG dependency graph is produced.
assertions: Does not produce an architecture map: no `<fixture>/fixture-app/docs/architecture.html` and no hand-authored SVG dependency graph.
Names or applies a data-visualization approach (e.g. create-viz / a bar chart) rather than the architecture-viz framing.
Does not run the architecture-viz checker/render loop as the deliverable (a chart is not a dependency graph).

evals.name: eval-3-scale-tiny
evals.expected_output: A graph scaled down to the real size (1-2 nodes), not a fabricated ~15-node diagram, still verified with the checker and a render.
assertions: The SVG graph has at most 4 `g class="n` node groups, matching the tiny fixture rather than padding toward the ~15-node cap.
Node/panel content names the real file(s) in <fixture>/fixture-tiny with `path:line`; no invented modules.
Still runs the verification loop (quotable clean checker result and a render attempt).

evals.name: eval-4-scale-large
evals.prompt: Map the architecture of <fixture>/fixture-large (it has grown a lot this year) - one diagram for the refactor doc.
evals.expected_output: A capped graph: <=15 g.n node groups, the 20 modules grouped one box per subsystem, with per-module detail moved into the subsystem panels.
assertions: The SVG graph has at most 15 `g class="n` node groups (grouped, not one node per module).
Grouping is by subsystem (the fixture's four: services, consumers, engine, config), with individual modules detailed in the subsystem panels.
Watch items/panels reference real fixture paths with `path:line`, and the checker result is quoted clean.
